key_insight: Applying a Laplacian-of-Gaussian enhancement together with a Gaussian-scale axis yields a G-LoG bi-filtration that captures boundary- and scale-aware topological features from volumetric medical images, with provable stability for multiparameter persistence representations.
problem_solved: Standard single-parameter filtrations miss scale-dependent boundary information in medical volumes; this work provides a practical, stable multiparameter filtration that better encodes geometric/topological features for classification.
method: Model volumetric medical images as bounded functions and apply a Laplacian-of-Gaussian (LoG) operator across Gaussian scales to enhance boundaries.
Construct a two-parameter (G-LoG) bi-filtration using Gaussian scale and LoG response, then compute multiparameter persistence summaries suited for multi-parameter persistence modules.
Prove an interleaving/stability result for the bi-filtration and convert multiparameter topological summaries into features for downstream classifiers (e.g., ML models for diagnosis).
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a theoretically grounded, boundary-aware topological feature extractor for 3D medical images that can improve robustness and interpretability of classification models—especially valuable when geometric detail and scale matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input volumetric scan → Gaussian scale axis + LoG operator → G-LoG bi-filtration → multiparameter persistence summary → classifier.
Side-by-side image slices: original vs. LoG-enhanced to show boundary amplification across scales.
Heatmap / contour of the bi-filtration domain and example Betti-number surface or multiparameter persistence summary visualization.
Bar/ROC chart comparing classification performance (or robustness) with and without G-LoG features.
paper_title: G-LoG Bi-filtration for Medical Image Classification
paper_authors: Qingsong Wang, Jiaxing He, Bingzhe Hou, Tieru Wu, Yang Cao
